cohort: The study included 10,598 BCG-vaccinated newborns from Guinea-Bissau, whose mothers' BCG scar status was inspected at enrolment.
finding: Among BCG-vaccinated newborns, maternal BCG priming (indicated by a scar) was associated with a trend for fewer in-hospital deaths from infection, particularly sepsis, within the first 6 weeks of life, with a stronger effect observed in males.
